title: Observability Sanctuary: keyed TTL + just-in-time unmasking for sensitive telemetry
creator: Ava Patel
description: Implement a tenant-aware "Sanctuary" layer for observability streams that enforces keyed TTLs, encrypted salted identifiers, and a just-in-time unmasking workflow for authorized audits. The feature targets traces, error logs, and latency telemetry and must integrate with RBAC and the audit ledger so reveal actions are recorded with a proof token.
background: We currently have coarse retention controls and field-level scrubbing in the pipeline, but customers (and internal compliance) ask for tenant-scoped TTLs keyed to contract tier, the ability to reveal sanitized fields for incident investigations under strict audit, and cryptographic gating so raw sensitive tokens are not persistently available. Existing tickets touched parts of this: trace replay controls (ENG-41207) and adaptive masking prototypes, but there is no unified enforcement layer or migration plan.
goals: Add per-tenant keyed TTL policy enforcement on observability streams (traces, error logs, latency histograms)
Store only pseudonymized identifiers by default; enable JIT unmasking for authorized principals with short-lived reveal tokens
Emit immutable audit entries for every unmask/reveal action to the access ledger and surface in Console (per-tenant view)
Provide migration scripts and backfill plan for telemetry within retention windows
Keep end-to-end P95 ingestion latency increase < 5% for typical workloads
out_of_scope: Full productized consent flows for end-user opt-out (separate legal project)
Reworking all historical dashboards to use pseudonymized IDs (we will provide tools but not change dashboards automatically)
Onboarding new KMS providers beyond existing HSM integration
acceptance_criteria: Per-tenant TTL enforcement exists and is configurable via Console and API
Default storage contains pseudonymized identifiers; real identifiers are never stored without an explicit reveal token
Reveal flow issues a short-lived cryptographic token tied to a CA-logged access request; all reveals generate audit entries with who/why/when
RBAC policy evaluation integrated: only principals with 'telemetry:reveal' scope can request unmasking; integration tests simulate policy changes
Performance: end-to-end ingestion P95 latency regression < 5% on benchmark harness
Migration: backfill script runs on a sample tenant and completes within the established data window; documented rollback plan

risks: Reveal flow complexity could be abused if RBAC rules are misconfigured; mitigation: default deny + automated policy linting
Pseudonymization collisions under high-cardinality IDs; mitigation: use tenant-scoped salts with collision detection metrics
Storage cost increase if TTLs are extended for many tenants; mitigation: quota alerts and cost-optimization playbook
Performance regression at ingestion hot paths; mitigation: staged rollout and performance gates in CI
